title: Rescuers search for thousands following deadly Nepal-China flood - CBC
description: Rescuers search for thousands following deadly Nepal-China flood  CBC
publisher.title: CBC
full_article:
As rescue efforts in communities buried by catastrophic flash floods along the border between Nepal and China entered their fourth day on Saturday, authorities continued finding survivors and transporting them to safety.

At relief centres, as some arrive, families wait anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of people unaccounted for continued to rise.

Chinese authorities have reported seven deaths and more than 550 missing, while Nepal's disaster agency said the death toll had climbed to 669 with 2,426 people missing.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far.

WATCH | Nepal-Tibet flash flood death toll continues to climb: Nepal-Tibet flash flood death toll climbs as fears of 2nd flood grow August 28 | Duration 2:21 CBC News is on the ground in Nepal, where fears are growing that a swollen artificial lake formed by this week's massive flash flood along the Tibet border could cause another flooding disaster. So far at least 579 people have been confirmed dead, while almost 2,000 are still missing.

In Nuwakot, one of the Nepali districts devastated by the floods, helicopters resumed operations before noon on Saturday after poor weather temporarily hampered aerial rescue activities.

Some helicopters were loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice. Others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors.

Villagers return to devastated homes

As people were still leaving Trishuli, some village residents were returning to see what could be salvaged from their decimated homes.

One boy walked out of the village carrying muddy sandals from his house. A woman, Shoba Shrestha, returned to find her dog, Sweetie, whom she was forced to leave behind when the floods came. Shrestha sat on the ground petting her and feeding her water from a bottle.

At some point, relief co-ordinators cleared villagers, reporters and volunteers from the entrance to Trishuli, as excavation equipment drove into the flooded village to dig.

Shoba Shrestha gives water to her dog, Sweetie, after the dog returned home on Saturday following four days apart in the aftermath of flash floods in Nepal's Nuwakot district. (Dar Yasin/The Associated Press)

Families begin to lose hope

In Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, relatives and friends gathered outside the main government hospital from early morning, desperately searching for news of missing loved ones.

Many shuffled between the help desk and the hospital notice board, clutching photographs and scanning injured patients' lists in the hope of finding them.

Dil Maya Lama stood weeping outside the help desk at the hospital, searching for information about her missing 26-year-old brother, a driver for a hydropower company in Rasuwa. She had travelled from Ramechhap, about 130 kilometres.

"I came here with the hope that I might find him," she said. "There is no information about him."

WATCH | Families of Canadians missing following flood still have hope: Families of Canadians missing in Nepal-Tibet flood cling to hope August 28 | Duration 1:55 Families of Canadians missing after the Nepal-Tibet flash flood disaster are desperate for any news of their loved ones, with some planning to travel to join the search efforts. Of the 32 Canadians reported missing, none have yet been confirmed dead.

Families covered hospital walls with posters showing missing relatives, photographs and contact numbers in a desperate appeal for any clue that could bring them home.

Nearby were photographs of unidentified bodies that officials put up in hopes they could be recognized by families or friends.

Gajendra Rawat, a security official at the hospital help desk, said families had so far registered about 1,600 missing persons since the disaster struck. "People are coming from all parts of Nepal," he said.

Back in Nuwakot, military personnel taped sheets of paper listing dozens of missing people to a wall at a relief centre, prompting families to crowd around them. Some scanned lists of the missing and dead, took photos and wiped away tears as they looked through the names.

Rajesh Kumar Ram desperately searched a list for his son's name.

"I'm hopeful, by chance, that my son is somewhere," he said, crying as he spoke. "Maybe they find him stuck somewhere. I'm waiting for that moment only."

Rescuers battle to find survivors in disaster-hit areas

Search-and-rescue efforts continued at several locations in Nepal and Tibet, including the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Nepal's Rasuwa district and the severely damaged Gyirong border crossing on the Chinese side.

Nepali army spokesperson Brig.-Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said rescue efforts would continue at the hydropower construction site, where authorities believe more than 100 people are trapped in a tunnel filled with thick mud.

Basnet said rescuers had used baskets and ropes to reach some people, but the operation remained difficult.

People crowd around to look at photographs of those killed in flash floods displayed outside a hospital to help relatives identify the victims, in Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, on Friday. (Dar Yasin/The Associated Press)

He said rescue teams had also been forced to relocate temporarily when authorities issued warnings about possible further flooding.

Rescuers have been on high alert for more flooding from a new lake that formed high up in the Himalayan mountains after the initial floods on Wednesday. Experts warned that the lake, created after a glacier collapse that triggered the floods, was starting to overflow.

Audio The disaster in Nepal as a ‘wake-up call from Mother Nature’

Monitoring data from the Chinese Ministry of Water Resources showed late Friday that the lake had dwindled in size. The water level dropped by 10 metres from a high point on Thursday morning, Chinese broadcaster CCTV said.

Aid trucks could be seen traveling from Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, toward the affected areas.

Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said on social media Saturday that a Canadian who was previously missing has been found safe.

Anand said there are still 31 Canadians still unaccounted for, noting the figure could still "fluctuate" as information becomes available.

Search continues at devastated China-Nepal border

The Chinese broadcaster showed images on Saturday of rescuers arriving at Gyirong Port, the hard-hit border crossing with Nepal. Some reached the area by foot or via rafts, while others dropped down from drones flown to the area. "Anyone, anyone?" rescuers yelled.

It was not immediately known how many people were at the border checkpoint building when the floods hit.

In this photo released by Xinhua News Agency, a drone carries cargo as search-and-rescue operations are underway at the mudslide-hit area in Gyirong County on Saturday. (Jiang Fan/Xinhua/The Associated Press)

On Saturday, Nepal's disaster agency said the death toll had climbed to 626, with 2,426 people missing in the country. More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far.

The death toll in China rose to seven on Friday as state media showed evacuations of villages and leaders' efforts to direct the relief response. China's state media said 554 people were missing on the Chinese side. Hundreds of the missing are foreigners who were in the area to work, trek or make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak.

कनाडा के विदेश मंत्री अनिता आनंद शनिदिन सोशल मीडिया पर कहलनि जे, पहिने लापता एकटा कनाडाई सुरक्षित भेटल अछि।

आनंद नँ कहलकै कि अभी भी ३१ कनाडाई के हिसाब नै छै, आरू ई बात के ध्यान रखतें हुअय कि जानकारी उपलब्ध होय के साथ-साथ ई आंकड़ा मँ अखनी भी “उतार-चढ़ाव” आबी सकै छै ।

तबाह चीन-नेपाल सीमा पर खोज जारी अछि

चीनी प्रसारक नेपालक संग कड़ा प्रभावित सीमा क्रासिंग ग्यिरॉंग बन्दरगाह पर पहुँचल बचावकर्मीक तस्वीर शनिदिन देखौलक। कियो पैदल या बेड़ा के माध्यम सं एहि इलाका मे पहुंचल छल, त कियो एहि इलाका मे उड़ाओल गेल ड्रोन सं नीचा उतरि गेल छल. "कियो, कियो?" बचावकर्मी चिचिया उठल।

बाढ़ि के समय सीमा नाका भवन मे कतेक लोक छल से तत्काल पता नहि चलल।

सिन्हुआ न्यूज एजेंसी द्वारा जारी ई फोटो म॑ ड्रोन माल ढुलाई करी रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि शनिदिन ग्योरॉंग काउंटी केरऽ कीचड़ स॑ प्रभावित इलाका म॑ खोज-बचाव अभियान चलैलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । (जियांग फैन/सिन्हुआ/द एसोसिएटेड प्रेस)

शनिदिन नेपालक आपदा एजेन्सी जनौलक अछि जे मृतकक संख्या ६२६ भऽ गेल अछि, जाहिमे देशमे २४२६ गोटे लापता अछि । नेपालमे एखन धरि ३७०० सँ बेसी लोकके उद्धार भेल अछि ।

चीन म॑ शुक्रवार क॑ मृतकऽ के संख्या सात होय गेलै, कैन्हेंकि सरकारी मीडिया न॑ गाँवऽ क॑ खाली करै के काम आरू नेता सिनी के राहत प्रतिक्रिया क॑ निर्देशित करै के कोशिश देखैलकै । चीन के सरकारी मीडिया के कहनाय छनि जे चीनी पक्ष सं 554 लोक लापता अछि. सैकड़ों लापता विदेशी छथि जे एहि इलाका मे काज करय लेल, ट्रेकिंग करय लेल या कोनो पवित्र चोटी के तीर्थ यात्रा करय लेल आयल छलाह.

title: Pope Leo prays for victims of devastating Nepal floods - Vatican News
description: Pope Leo prays for victims of devastating Nepal floods  Vatican News
publisher.title: Vatican News
full_article:
Vatican News

Pope Leo XIV has expressed his deep sorrow over the loss of life and widespread devastation caused by flash floods in Nepal.

In a telegram sent on Thursday and signed by Cardinal Secretary of State Pietro Parolin, the Pope commended the souls of those who died “to the clemency of the Almighty” and offered his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved.

He also assured all those affected by the disaster of his spiritual closeness and prayed for the emergency personnel engaged in the ongoing search-and-rescue operations.

The telegram concluded with the Pope's prayers for God’s assistance and protection upon the people of Nepal.

Hundreds dead or missing

Over 350 people have died in Nepal, while more than 900 remain unaccounted for after a devastating torrent of water, mud and debris swept through communities near the country’s northern border with China. Unfortunately, the death toll is expected to rise as bodies are recovered from under the debris.

Hundreds more are missing in neighbouring Tibet, bringing the total number of people unaccounted for across the affected region to almost 1,500.

The disaster is believed to have been triggered by the collapse of part of a Himalayan glacier, which sent a sudden surge into a river system along the Nepal-China border. Scientists said the force of the collapse was so great that the resulting tremors were initially mistaken for an earthquake.

Entire settlements were inundated, while roads, bridges, power installations and other essential infrastructure were destroyed or severely damaged. The floods also struck a major border crossing, cutting off transport and trade routes.

Many of those missing are foreign visitors who had travelled to the region on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar, sites considered sacred by Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and followers of the Bon religion.

Rescue operations continue

Thousands of soldiers, police officers and emergency workers have been deployed across the affected areas. Helicopters are being used to reach isolated communities, evacuate survivors and deliver food, medical supplies and other forms of emergency assistance.

Operations are being complicated by damaged roads, difficult mountainous terrain and the continuing danger of landslides and further flooding.

International aid has begun to arrive, with neighbouring countries, the United Nations and humanitarian organisations offering personnel, supplies and financial assistance.

The tragedy has also renewed concerns about the growing threat posed by glacial instability in the Himalayas, where rising temperatures are accelerating the melting and retreat of glaciers.

पोप लियो चौदहवाँ नेपालमे झटका बाढ़ि सँ भेल जान-हानि आ व्यापक तबाही पर गहींर दुख व्यक्त केने छथि ।

गुरुवार क॑ भेजलऽ गेलऽ आरू कार्डिनल विदेश सचिव पिएत्रो पैरोलिन केरऽ हस्ताक्षर वाला तार म॑ पोप न॑ “सर्वशक्तिमान केरऽ दया” म॑ मरै वाला लोगऽ के आत्मा के प्रशंसा करलकै आरू शोक संतप्त लोगऽ के प्रति दिल स॑ संवेदना व्यक्त करलकै ।

आपदा स॑ प्रभावित सब लोगऽ क॑ अपनऽ आध्यात्मिक निकटता के आश्वासन भी देलकै आरू जारी खोज-बचाव अभियान म॑ जुटलऽ आपातकालीन कर्मी सिनी लेली प्रार्थना करलकै ।

तार केरऽ समापन पोप केरऽ नेपाल केरऽ जनता प॑ भगवान केरऽ सहायता आरू सुरक्षा केरऽ प्रार्थना स॑ करलऽ गेलै ।

सैकड़ों मृत या लापता

चीन के साथ देश के उत्तरी सीमा के पास समुदायऽ म॑ पानी, थाल आरू मलबा के विनाशकारी धार बहला के बाद नेपाल म॑ ३५० स॑ अधिक लोगऽ के मौत होय चुकलऽ छै, जबकि ९०० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के हिसाब नै छै । दुर्भाग्यवश मलबा के नीचा सं लाश बरामद भेला सं मृतक के संख्या बढ़य के उम्मीद अछि.

पड़ोसी देश तिब्बत म॑ सैकड़ों आरू लोगऽ के लापता छै, जेकरा स॑ पूरा प्रभावित क्षेत्र म॑ बेहिसाब लोगऽ के संख्या लगभग १५०० होय गेलऽ छै ।

मानल जा रहल अछि जे ई आपदा हिमालयी ग्लेशियर के किछु हिस्सा के ढहला सं भेल अछि, जाहि सं नेपाल-चीन सीमा पर नदी प्रणाली मे अचानक उफान आबि गेल. वैज्ञानिक सब के कहनाय छनि जे एहि गिरय के बल एतेक बेसी छल जे एकर परिणामस्वरूप बनल भूकंप के शुरू मे भूकंप के गलती सं मानल गेल छल.

पूरा बस्ती बाढ़ि मे आबि गेल, जखन कि सड़क, पुल, बिजली स्थापना आ अन्य आवश्यक बुनियादी ढांचा नष्ट भ गेल या गंभीर रूप स क्षतिग्रस्त भ गेल। बाढ़ि के कारण एकटा पैघ सीमा क्रासिंग सेहो आबि गेल अछि, जाहि सं परिवहन आ व्यापारिक मार्ग बंद भ गेल.

लापता लोगऽ म॑ स॑ बहुत सारा विदेशी आगंतुक छै जे हिन्दू, बौद्ध, जैन आरू बोन धर्म के अनुयायी सिनी द्वारा पवित्र मानलऽ जाय वाला स्थल कैलाश पर्वत आरू मानसरोवर झील के तीर्थयात्रा प॑ ई क्षेत्र गेलऽ छेलै ।

बचाव कार्य जारी अछि

प्रभावित इलाका मे हजारों जवान, पुलिस अधिकारी आ आपातकालीन कार्यकर्ता के तैनाती कायल गेल अछि। हेलीकॉप्टर के उपयोग अलग-थलग समुदाय तक पहुंचै, बची गेलऽ लोगऽ क॑ बाहर निकालै आरू भोजन, चिकित्सा आपूर्ति आरू अन्य तरह के आपातकालीन सहायता पहुँचै लेली करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

सड़क क्षतिग्रस्त, कठिन पहाड़ी इलाका आ भूस्खलन आ आओर बाढ़ि के लगातार खतरा के कारण परिचालन जटिल भ रहल अछि.

अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सहायता केरऽ आगमन शुरू होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ पड़ोसी देश, संयुक्त राष्ट्र आरू मानवीय संगठन कर्मी, आपूर्ति आरू आर्थिक सहायता के पेशकश करी रहलऽ छै ।

ई त्रासदी न॑ हिमालय म॑ हिमनदी अस्थिरता के वजह स॑ बढ़तऽ खतरा के बारे म॑ भी चिंता क॑ नवीनीकरण करी देल॑ छै, जहां बढ़तऽ तापमान स॑ ग्लेशियरऽ के पिघलना आरू पीछे हटै म॑ तेजी आबी रहलऽ छै ।

HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - Hawaii’s Nepalese community is closely monitoring catastrophic flooding in Nepal.

More than 600 people are confirmed dead after flooding near the China border, while about 2,500 people, including Americans and other foreign nationals, remain missing.

Experts believe the disaster may have been caused by a glacier collapse.

Dinesh Timilsina, president of the Society of Nepalese in Hawaii, said the tragedy is hitting the local community hard.

“So this tragedy feels very personal,” Timilsina said. “Right now I think the community focuses on rescue and finding those who are still missing and making sure the survivors have plenty of food, shelter and basic necessities.”

He called it a difficult and emotional time for the community.

The Society of Nepalese in Hawaii said it is continuing to monitor the situation and plans to share ways the community can support relief efforts in Nepal.

title: Nepal flood death toll nears 700, with more than 3,000 missing, as poor weather hampers rescues - CBS News
description: Nepal flood death toll nears 700, with more than 3,000 missing, as poor weather hampers rescues  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
The death toll from Wednesday's devastating flash floods in Nepal and along the border with China has risen to nearly 700, with around 3,000 people still missing, as rescue operations entered their fourth day.

The combined toll in Nepal and Tibet, an autonomous region in China, rose to 691 dead and over 3,000 people missing after China's latest update on Sunday.

Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing, while Nepal's disaster agency said late Saturday that the death toll had climbed to 675 with 2,498 people missing.

Poor weather and challenging terrain have hampered aerial rescue operations.

In Nuwakot, one of the Nepali districts devastated by the floods, helicopters resumed operations before noon Saturday after poor weather temporarily obstructed their activities. Some helicopters were loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice. Others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors.

An aerial view shows debris and mud covering settlements following flash floods on Aug. 28, 2026, in DevGhat village, Nepal. Ritesh Shukla / Getty Images

Families of the missing have been waiting for news of loved ones outside an army camp near Nuwakot.

A Nepali Army official told CBS News that its search and rescue helicopters could do a combined 15 trips an hour back and forth into the disaster zone, for a total of about 500 trips per day. Each flight is bringing in a handful of people, some carried out by stretcher.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far, according to authorities there. Hundreds of the missing are foreigners who were in the area to work, trek or make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak on the Tibet side of the border.

Amid the frantic search for survivors, Nepal issued a warned Sunday morning local time of further rising flood waters.

"We have received information that the flood flow in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa has increased further," the country's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said in an alert obtained by Agence France-Presse.

"Therefore, all personnel engaged in search, rescue, and relief operations, those in riverside areas, and everyone else in affected areas including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, and Chitwan are requested to exercise caution."

The U.S. State Department, meanwhile, said in a social media post Saturday that it was providing more than $3.6 million in humanitarian aid to Nepal, which would include three months of emergency food assistance designed to help up to 10,000 households.

Authorities search for dozens trapped in tunnels

Nepal's government says more than 100 workers may still be alive and trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects, with rescue efforts focused on the Trishuli 3A and 3B sites. Initial reports suggested the 100 trapped were in a single location, but Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said "rescue efforts are going on in multiple tunnel sites." Rescuers managed to reach some people with helicopter baskets and ropes, but struggled with 4 to 5 feet of mud and limited landing sites, Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said.

On Saturday, rescuers broke through the mud at Trishuli 3A. They were able to begin sending air into the tunnel, and excavation efforts are underway, Nepali Home Minister Sudan Gurung. The Ministry of Energy reported efforts to send a camera into the tunnel have begun.

Specialized Indian and Chinese tunnel-rescue teams have joined the effort to free the trapped workers. India has extensive experience with difficult Himalayan tunnel rescues, including teams of "rat-hole" miners skilled in being able to crawl into narrow spaces. Nepal's expert mountain rescue teams — used to aiding climbers on the world's highest peaks, including Everest — are also joining the search for the missing.

Photographs shared by Nepal's disaster office showed workers wading through churned mud and navigating vast boulders left by the floods.

Priti Kharel said she believes her brother Milan is one of those trapped. He works as an engineering geologist at Doosan Enerbility, and his family has not heard from him since the floods. Kharel said friends who were at the site told her family that Milan might still be there.

"It's already four days," Kharel said. "We want the government to rescue him as soon as possible."

A woman walks through mud and debris left behind by flash flooding in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh) Rajesh Kumar Singh

Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said locating those still missing is "currently our national priority." He said Nepal's government has sought specialized support from neighbors for tunnel rescue, survivor-detection technology, rapid forensic and DNA analysis, and morgue refrigerators.

Khanal said an 11-member tunnel rescue reconnaissance team from India has been deployed, while a similar rescue team from China is expected shortly, he added.

Families search for information

At relief centers, families are waiting anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of those missing continue to rise. Others scour hospitals and paper lists for any signs of hope.

In Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, relatives and friends gathered outside the main government hospital from early morning, desperately searching for news of missing loved ones. Many shuffled between the help desk and the hospital notice board, clutching photographs and scanning injured patients' lists in the hope of finding them.

Families covered hospital walls with posters showing missing relatives, photographs and contact numbers in a desperate appeal for any clue that could bring them home. Nearby were photographs of unidentified bodies that officials put up in hopes families or friends could recognize them.

Gajendra Rawat, a security official at the hospital help desk, said families had so far registered around 1,600 missing persons since the disaster struck.

"People are coming from all parts of Nepal," he said.

Residents carry their belongings salvaged from their damaged homes filled with mud and debris in Devighat, in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026, following the Aug. 26 flash floods. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh) Rajesh Kumar Singh

Dil Maya Lama stood weeping outside the help desk at the hospital, searching for information about her missing 26-year-old brother, a driver for a hydropower company in Rasuwa. She had traveled from Ramechhap, about 80 miles away.

"I came here with the hope that I might find him," she said. "There is no information about him."

Nelza Moktan anxiously sought information about her missing cousin, who also worked as a driver in Rasuwa.

"I feel hopeless. It has already been four days," she said.

Back in Nuwakot, military personnel taped sheets of paper listing dozens of missing people to a wall at a relief center, prompting families to crowd around them. Some scanned lists of the missing and dead, took photos and wiped away tears. Rajesh Kumar Ram, who is searching for his son, desperately searched a list for his son's name.

"I'm hopeful, by chance, that my son is somewhere," he said, crying as he spoke. "Maybe they find him stuck somewhere. I'm waiting for that moment only."

The Red Cross said Friday that some 90,000 people had likely been impacted by the flooding. Khanal said Nepal has received over 57 metric tons of relief supplies from India, with additional aid arriving from China, Japan, Australia and other countries. Khanal added that further support will be sought as needs assessments continue.

In this photo released by Xinhua News Agency, rescuers carry out search and rescue operations at the mudslide-hit area in Gyirong County, southwest China's Tibet Autonomous Region on Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (Zheng Lijun/Xinhua via AP) Zheng Lijun

Authorities wary of further flood risk

Rescuers have been on high alert for more flooding from a new lake that formed high up in the Himalayan mountains after the initial floods on Wednesday. Experts warned that the lake, created after the glacier collapse that triggered the floods, was starting to overflow.

Basnet said rescue teams had been forced to relocate temporarily when authorities issued warnings about possible further flooding.

Monitoring data from the Chinese Ministry of Water Resources showed late Friday that the lake had dwindled in size. The water level dropped by 32 feet from its high point on Thursday morning, Chinese broadcaster CCTV said.

Scientists said satellite images indicated that the initial flooding was caused when bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event. The rocks and melted water suddenly swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing torrents of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria who is currently based in Bangladesh, said "a lower part of a glacier has really come off."

Satellite images show a valley of the Langtang Lirung mountain peak in Nepal on June 25, 2026, and Aug. 26, 2026, when devastating flooding struck the country. Sabrina Blanchard and Luca Matteucci/AFP via Getty Images

The Hindu Kush Himalayan region is warming rapidly , driving major changes in glaciers, snow cover, permafrost and mountain slopes, according to climate scientists. Around 78% of the glacier area, located between about 14,760 and 19,685 feet above sea level, is highly exposed to warming.

"What happened yesterday is unfortunately the new normal. It's going to get worse from here onwards," Steiner said.

Khanal said in a statement obtained by AFP that he spoke by phone his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, and both agreed to increase the sharing of "real-time hydrological data."

Wang, in a Chinese foreign ministry statement obtained by AFP, said Beijing had "shared crucial information with Nepal, including disaster area imagery, satellite and hydrological data, as well as early warnings about upstream barrier lakes."

Wang added that "China and Nepal are bound by mountains and rivers, sharing a common destiny."

Khanal earlier told reporters that Nepal needed greater research to "understand the changing dynamics of the Himalayan ecosystem," and the risks they pose to the landlocked country, encircled by India and China, AFP reported.

Americans among the missing

Five Americans have made their way to safety, and around 90 are among those unaccounted for, the U.S. State Department said Friday.

In a statement, the U.S. Embassy in Nepal said the U.S. was "delivering a range of supplies requested by the Government of Nepal and is working with Nepal to ensure that assistance reaches the people who need it."

"Catholic Relief Services, working through implementing partner Caritas Nepal, will deliver more than 2.5 metric tons of food supplies, 500 blankets, 500 mosquito nets, and 500 insulating foam sheets for temporary shelter flooring to two school locations in Rasuwa," the embassy said, noting plans for subsequent supply shipments were already in place.

Twenty-two people from the U.S. were among the 80 who went missing from a pilgrimage run by the Isha Foundation, a volunteer-run group that promotes well-being founded by Indian spiritual leader Sadhguru Vasudev.

"At this point we are awaiting word," community liaison Leslie Crespi said in a phone interview from McMinnville, Tennessee, of the missing pilgrims. "We have done as much outreach as we can through the State Department, through the embassy."

The 22 missing Americans were all adults, and included 13 women and nine men, the foundation later said in data it provided to CBS News. She said the Isha Foundation has organized pilgrimages for 21 years, and "in those 21 years, we have never lost a life."

U.S. citizen Deepak Dandu said his wife, Sridevi Vejella, was among those missing in Nepal. She was on the pilgrimage with the Isha Foundation to Mount Kailash in Tibet — a sacred site for Hindus, Buddhists and others — which he said was a "lifelong dream" for her.

Extensive destruction and debris deposits along the Trishuli River corridor following a catastrophic outburst flood and debris flow in Bidur, Nuwakot district, Nepal, on Aug. 28, 2026. Sameer Shrestha/Anadolu via Getty Images

He told CBS News she was crossing from China into Nepal when the flood hit. The foundation told him she was part of a group that was present at the Gyirong Port immigration complex.

President Trump called the flooding terrible to see on Thursday, saying that "strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks."

He told reporters in the Oval Office that U.S. officials had spoken with Nepalese leaders and offered to provide "anything they want."

Ramy Inocencio contributed to this report.

बुधदिन नेपाल आ चीन सीमा पर भेल विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ि मे मृतकक संख्या लगभग 700 भ गेल अछि, जखन कि लगभग 3000 लोक एखनो लापता अछि, जखन कि बचाव अभियान चारिम दिन मे प्रवेश केलक अछि।

चीन केरऽ स्वायत्त क्षेत्र नेपाल आरू तिब्बत म॑ रविवार क॑ चीन केरऽ ताजा अपडेट के बाद कुल मिला क॑ ६९१ लोगऽ के मौत आरू ३,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के लापता होय गेलऽ छै ।

चीन के अधिकारी 16 के मौत आ 546 लोक के लापता होय के सूचना देलक अछि, जखन कि नेपाल के आपदा एजेंसी शनिदिन देर राति मे कहलक अछि जे मृतक के संख्या 675 भ गेल अछि जाहि मे 2498 लोक लापता अछि।

खराब मौसम आ चुनौतीपूर्ण इलाका के कारण हवाई बचाव कार्य में बाधा पहुंचल अछि.

बाढ़ि सँ तबाह नेपाली जिल्ला मे सँ एक नुवाकोट मे शनिदिन दुपहर सँ पहिने हेलीकॉप्टर के परिचालन शुरू भ गेल, जखन कि खराब मौसम के कारण अस्थायी तौर पर ओकर गतिविधि मे बाधा आबि गेल। किछु हेलीकॉप्टर मे कपड़ा, इंस्टेंट नूडल्स, पटाखा आ चावल सहित सहायताक बक्सा आ बैग लदल छल। दोसर लोक बाढ़ि प्रभावित इलाका स बचि गेल लोक कए ल कए वापस आबि गेल।

हवाई दृश्य में नेपाल के देवघाट गाम में 28 अगस्त 2026 के आकस्मिक बाढ़ के बाद बस्ती के ढकने मलबा आ कीचड़ देखल गेल अछि। रितेश शुक्ला / गेटी इमेजेज

लापता के परिवार नुवाकोट के पास सेना के कैंप के बाहर अपन प्रियजन के खबर के इंतजार में रहल अछि.

नेपाली सेना केरऽ एगो अधिकारी न॑ सीबीएस न्यूज क॑ बतैलकै कि ओकरऽ खोज आरू बचाव हेलीकॉप्टर आपदा क्षेत्र म॑ एक घंटा म॑ मिल क॑ १५ यात्रा करी क॑ आगू-पीछू करी सकै छै, जेकरा स॑ कुल प्रतिदिन लगभग ५०० यात्रा होय सकै छै । प्रत्येक फ्लाइट मे मुट्ठी भरि लोक आबि रहल अछि, किछु स्ट्रेचर सं सेहो कएल जा रहल अछि.

नेपालमे एखन धरि ३,७०० सँ बेसी लोकके उद्धार कएल गेल अछि, ओतयके अधिकारी जनौलक अछि । सैकड़ों लापता विदेशी छथि जे एहि इलाका मे काज करय लेल, ट्रेकिंग करय लेल या सीमा के तिब्बत कात कोनो पवित्र चोटी पर यात्रा करय लेल आयल छलाह.

बचे वाला के उन्मादी खोज के बीच नेपाल रविदिन भोर स्थानीय समय के अनुसार बाढ़ के पानि आओर बढ़य के चेतावनी जारी केलक अछि.

देश केरऽ राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम कम करै आरू प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण न॑ एजेंसी फ्रांस-प्रेस क॑ मिललऽ अलर्ट म॑ कहलकै कि हमरा सब क॑ ई जानकारी मिललै कि रसुवा केरऽ भोटेकोशी नदी म॑ बाढ़ के बहाव आरू बढ़ी गेलऽ छै ।

"अतः खोज, बचाव, आरू राहत कार्य मँ जुटलऽ सब कर्मी, नदी के किनारे के क्षेत्र मँ जुटलऽ सब कर्मी, आरू रसुवा, नुवाकोट, धडिंग, आरू चितवन सहित प्रभावित क्षेत्र मँ सब लोग स॑ आग्रह करलऽ जाय छै कि वू सावधानी बरतै ।"

ओतहि अमेरिकी विदेश विभाग शनिदिन सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट मे कहलनि जे, ओ नेपाल केँ 36 लाख डॉलर सँ बेसी के मानवीय सहायता द रहल अछि, जाहि मे तीन महीना के आपातकालीन खाद्य सहायता शामिल होयत जे 10 हजार घर तक के मदद के लेल डिजाइन कयल गेल अछि।

अधिकारी सुरंग मे फंसल दर्जनों लोकक तलाश मे छथि

नेपाल सरकार के कहनाय छनि जे 100 सं बेसि मजदूर एखनो जीवित रहि सकैत अछि आओर जलविद्युत परियोजना मे सुरंग के भीतर फंसल भ सकैत अछि, जाहि मे बचाव के प्रयास त्रिशुली 3 ए आओर 3 बी स्थल पर केन्द्रित अछि. प्रारंभिक रिपोर्ट मे कहल गेल छल जे फंसल 100 लोक एकहि स्थान पर अछि, मुदा ऊर्जा मंत्री बिराज भक्त श्रेष्ठ कहला जे कईटा सुरंग स्थल पर बचाव क प्रयास चलि रहल अछि। बचावकर्मी हेलीकॉप्टर के टोकरी आ रस्सी ल क किछु लोक तक पहुंचय मे सफल रहल, मुदा 4 सं 5 फीट के थाल आ सीमित लैंडिंग साइट सं जूझि गेल, ब्रिगेडियर. जनरल राजा राम बस्नेत कहलनि।

शनिदिन त्रिशुली 3 ए मे बचावकर्मी थाल तोड़ि देलक। सुरंग में हवा भेजना शुरू करै में सफल रहलै, आरू खुदाई के प्रयास चलै छै, नेपाली गृहमंत्री सूडान गुरुंग । ऊर्जा मंत्रालय केरऽ रिपोर्ट छै कि सुरंग म॑ कैमरा भेजै के कोशिश शुरू होय गेलऽ छै ।

फंसल मजदूर कए मुक्त करबाक प्रयास मे विशेष भारतीय आ चीनी सुरंग-बचाव टीम सेहो शामिल भ गेल अछि। भारत क॑ हिमालयी सुरंगऽ के कठिन बचाव के व्यापक अनुभव छै, जेकरा म॑ "चूहा-छेद" वाला खननकर्ता के टीम भी शामिल छै जे संकीर्ण जगहऽ प॑ रेंगै म॑ सक्षम छै । नेपाल केरऽ विशेषज्ञ पर्वत बचाव टीम — जेकरा एवरेस्ट सहित दुनिया केरऽ सबसें ऊँचऽ चोटी प॑ पर्वतारोही सिनी के सहायता करै के आदत छै — भी लापता लोगऽ के खोज म॑ शामिल होय रहलऽ छै ।

नेपालक आपदा कार्यालय द्वारा साझा कएल गेल फोटो मे मजदूर मथल थाल मे डुबकी लगा कए बाढ़ि सँ छोड़ल विशाल बोल्डर मे घुमैत देखाओल गेल अछि ।

प्रीति खरेल कहलनि जे, हुनकर मानब अछि जे हुनकर भाई मिलन फंसल लोक मे सं एक छथि। दूसन एनरबिलिटी में इंजीनियरिंग भूवैज्ञानिक के काज करैत छथि, आ बाढ़ि के बाद सं हुनकर परिवार के कोनो खबर नहिं. खरेल कहलनि जे, एहि ठाम जे दोस्त छल ओ हुनकर परिवार के कहलक जे मिलन एखनो ओतय भ सकैत अछि।

खरेल कहलकै, "पहिने सँ चारि दिन भ' गेलै।" हम चाहैत छी जे सरकार हुनका जल्द स जल्द बचाबय।'

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला में झटका बाढ़ि के बाद छोड़ल गेल थाल आ मलबा के बीच स गुजरैत एकटा महिला, शनिदिन, 29 अगस्त 2026। (एपी फोटो/राजेश कुमार सिंह) राजेश कुमार सिंह

नेपाल के विदेश मंत्री शिसिर खनाल कहलनि जे, एखन धरि लापता लोक के पता लगाबय के काज “अखन हमर राष्ट्रीय प्राथमिकता” अछि। ओ कहलनि जे, नेपाल सरकार सुरंग बचाव, बचे वाला-डिटेक्शन तकनीक, रैपिड फोरेंसिक आ डीएनए एनालिसिस, आ मुर्दाघर फ्रिज के लेल पड़ोसी सं विशेष सहयोग मंगलक अछि।

खनाल नँ कहलकै कि भारत सँ ११ सदस्यीय सुरंग बचाव टोही टीम तैनात करलौ गेलौ छै, जबकि चीन सँ कुछ ही समय मँ ऐसनौ बचाव टीम के आबै के उम्मीद छै, हुनी आरू कहलकै ।

title: Bay Area families await word on loved ones missing in Nepal-Tibet floods - CBS News
description: Bay Area families await word on loved ones missing in Nepal-Tibet floods  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
More than 600 people have been confirmed dead and thousands remain missing after flash floods and mudslides along the Nepal-Tibet border , including dozens of Americans whose families are anxiously waiting for news.

Among those missing is a 48-year-old Milpitas father who works as an engineer for Santa Clara-based tech company Everpure, Inc., formerly known as Pure Storage.

Praneeth Sajepa said his older brother, Prabhath Sajeepa, was crossing from Tibet into Nepal on Wednesday morning as part of a large group traveling back from a holy pilgrimage.

Family members believe Prabhath may have been near a building that was swallowed by a flash flood at a major border crossing. Surveillance video shows people running as floodwaters engulf the building.

"All we want to figure out is whether he was inside the building, outside the building, or how far he was away from the building," Praneeth said.

Praneeth, speaking from India, said his brother lives in Milpitas and has two children. He said his brother is a naturalized U.S. citizen.

"It has been a very hard last couple of days," Praneeth said. "So it's been very tough to handle. And we have been going through a tough time right now."

He said watching the videos of the flooding has been difficult but that he has not given up hope.

"Going through those videos, it was very, very tough to digest," he said.

Everpure, Inc. said in a statement that it is working with authorities to locate Prabhath and support his family.

"We are doing everything within our power to support efforts to establish contact and locate Prabhath," the company wrote in a statement. "Our team is working continuously with local authorities, emergency services, and diplomatic officials to support search and rescue operations. Our immediate priority is supporting Prabhath's family during this incredibly difficult time."

Other Bay Area families are also waiting for information about loved ones who may have been caught in the disaster.

Jay Tamang of Marin County said he is searching for friends from the village where he grew up. He said people from his village and his wife's village are among those still missing.

"People from my village, and people from my wife's village, there are a lot of people still missing," Tamang said.

Communication has been difficult because of the disaster and damage to telecommunications infrastructure.

"At this point, due to lack of telecommunications, we really couldn't contact," Tamang said.

Another Bay Area family reached out to CBS News Bay Area about Sudhindra Yapalparvi, a missing father who lives in Virginia while his son and other relatives live in the Bay Area. The family said he was traveling with a group of U.S. tourists on a pilgrimage.

For the families waiting for word, hope remains their strongest source of comfort.

"We are hoping for some miracle to happen," Praneeth said.

He said he is prepared to travel to Tibet and Nepal once he receives more information about where search crews are looking for his brother.

The disaster has also prompted a response from the Bay Area's Nepali community. The U.S. Census shows thousands of Nepali families live in the East Bay, particularly in West Contra Costa County.

Dozens of people gathered Friday night at the Nepali Community Center in Richmond for a candlelight vigil honoring those killed or missing in the floods. Participants arranged candles on the ground to spell the word "PRAY."

title: Nepal-China flood survivors reach safe areas as families await news of nearly 3,000 missing - AP News
description: Nepal-China flood survivors reach safe areas as families await news of nearly 3,000 missing  AP News

full_article:
NUWAKOT, Nepal (AP) — As rescue efforts in communities buried by catastrophic flash floods along the Nepal - China border entered their fourth day Saturday, authorities were still finding survivors and transporting them to safety.

At relief centers, families of missing people waited anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of people unaccounted for continued to rise.

The combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 691 dead and over 3,000 people missing after China’s latest update on Sunday. Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, while Nepal’s disaster agency said late Saturday that the death toll had climbed to 675 with 2,498 people missing.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far.

In Nuwakot, one of the Nepali districts devastated by the floods, helicopters arrived loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice. Others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors.

Families begin to lose hope

In Kathmandu, Nepal’s capital, relatives and friends gathered outside the main government hospital from early morning, desperately searching for news of missing loved ones.

Many shuffled between the help desk and the hospital notice board, clutching photographs and scanning injured patients’ lists in the hope of finding them.

Dil Maya Lama stood weeping outside the help desk at the hospital, searching for information about her missing 26-year-old brother, a driver for a hydropower company in Rasuwa. She had traveled from Ramechhap, about 130 kilometers (80 miles) away.

“I came here with the hope that I might find him,” she said. “There is no information about him.”

Nelza Moktan anxiously sought information about her missing cousin, who also worked as a driver in Rasuwa.

“I feel hopeless. It has already been four days,” she said.

Families covered hospital walls with posters showing missing relatives, photographs and contact numbers in a desperate appeal for any clue that could bring them home.

Families search paper lists for any clue

Back in Nuwakot, military personnel taped sheets of paper listing dozens of missing people to a wall at a relief center.

Families crowded around to scan the names of the missing and dead, taking photos and wiping away tears.

Rajesh Kumar Ram desperately searched through a list for his son’s name.

“I’m hopeful, by chance, that my son is somewhere,” he said, crying as he spoke. “Maybe they find him stuck somewhere. I’m waiting for that moment only.”

Outside, people walked along mud-covered streets past signs of the disaster. On one street, a truck was stuck in the mud with its bed raised in the air.

Priti Kharel stood outside the entrance to the army barracks, holding a poster with a picture of her brother, Milan Kharel, who works as an engineering geologist at Doosan Enerbility. His family hasn’t heard from him since the floods.

“It’s already four days,” said Kharel, who believes his brother could be one of the people trapped inside the tunnel of a hydropower construction site, where authorities have rescued some people.

Rescuers battle to find survivors in disaster-hit areas

Search and rescue efforts continued at several locations in Nepal and China’s Tibet, including the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Nepal’s Rasuwa district and the severely damaged Gyirong border crossing on the Chinese side.

Nepali Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said rescue efforts would continue at the hydropower construction site, where authorities believe more than 100 people are trapped in a tunnel filled with thick mud.

Rescuers had been on high alert for more flooding from a new lake that formed high up in the Himalayan mountains after the initial floods Wednesday.

In a news briefing Saturday, Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said authorities have mobilized all available resources with support from international assistance for search, rescue, relief and recovery operations, with a particular focus on locating those still missing.

He said rescue operations are challenging because of steep, tall mountains and narrow gorges in the disaster-hit region.

Khanal said the government has sought specialized support from Nepal’s neighbors in tunnel rescue, survivor-detection technology, rapid forensic and DNA analysis, as well as morgue refrigerators.

An 11-member tunnel rescue reconnaissance team from India has been deployed while a similar rescue team from China is expected shortly, he added.

खड़ा पहाड़ आ संकीर्ण गॉर्ज बचाव कार्य मे बाधा उत्पन्न करैत अछि

शनिदिन एकटा न्यूज ब्रिफिंग मे नेपालक विदेश मंत्री शिसिर खनाल कहलनि जे, अधिकारि सब खोज, बचाव, राहत आ बरामदगी के काज लेल अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सहायता के सहयोग स उपलब्ध सब संसाधन के जुटा लेलक अछि, जाहि में एखन धरि लापता लोक के पता लगेबा पर विशेष ध्यान देल गेल अछि।

शनिदिन पत्रकार सब स बातचीत मे ओ कहला जे एखन इ हमर राष्ट्रीय प्राथमिकता अछि।

खनाल कहलनि जे, सरकार नेपाल के पड़ोसी देश सं सुरंग बचाव, बचे वाला के पता लगाबय के तकनीक, रैपिड फोरेंसिक आ डीएनए एनालिसिस के संग-संग मुर्दाघर के फ्रिज के विशेष सहयोग मांगने अछि।

हुनी आरू कहलकै कि भारत स॑ ११ सदस्यीय सुरंग बचाव टोही टीम क॑ तैनात करलऽ गेलऽ छै जबकि चीन स॑ भी ऐसनऽ ही बचाव टीम केरऽ आबै के उम्मीद छै ।

मंत्री कहलनि जे, नेपाल केँ भारत सँ ५७ मीट्रिक टन सँ बेसी राहत सामग्री भेटल अछि, जाहि मे चीन, जापान, ऑस्ट्रेलिया आ अन्य देश सँ अतिरिक्त सहायता पहुँचल अछि। ओ इहो कहलनि जे, आवश्यकताक आकलन जारी रहला पर आओर सहयोग मांगल जायत।

___ २.

काफ्ले नेपाल के काठमांडू से रिपोर्ट। मलेशिया के कुआलालंपुर में एसोसिएटेड प्रेस के पत्रकार इलीन एनजी; भारत के बेंगलुरु में सिबी अरसु; नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला में उपेन्द्र मानसिंह; भारत के नई दिल्ली में ऐजाज हुसैन; आरू वाशिंगटन केरऽ दीदी तांग न॑ ई रिपोर्ट म॑ योगदान देलकै ।

title: Families balance hope and despair in race to find survivors in Nepal as 41 Australians still missing - The Guardian
description: Families balance hope and despair in race to find survivors in Nepal as 41 Australians still missing  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
S ome of them are young, some old; most of them appear to be men. Some of them could be sleeping, except for the mud that covers their bodies. Some, it seems, would be impossible to recognise even if you knew them well.

Every few hours Nepalese authorities hang pictures of the deceased, who have not been identified, on a wall at the back of a teaching hospital in Kathmandu.

Saluja, a young woman who did not give her last name, stood among a group of more than 100 people watching. Her cousin, 31, was not on the wall that day.

“It’s very hard to identify their faces,” Saluja says.

As she speaks, some in the crowd take videos to send to other relatives; they stand around comparing them, trying to work out whether the person in the photo is their loved one. The bodies have a piece of paper lying on top of them, showing which district they were found in, with a number to contact.

“My cousin is missing,” Saluja says. “He worked in a hydro power plant … Since the flood, we have not been able to contact him.

“It was the first area to get affected, so we really don’t know. But we are hoping for the best.”

While she talked, her other cousin, his older brother, was on the plane flying home from Australia. Since Wednesday, Kathmandu has swelled with international visitors – not tourists but people looking for their loved ones.

The Nepalese government has deployed about 15,000 personnel – from the army to the police – to move up the valley and into the areas decimated by the flood, hoping to find survivors.

View image in fullscreen A drone view of the aftermath of flash flooding at the confluence of the Trishuli and Tadi rivers in the Nuwakot district, Nepal. Photograph: Rajesh Kumar Singh/AP

While they battle arduous search conditions – areas completely cut off, roads destroyed, bridges washed away and a new lake threatening to burst – loved ones from Australia rush to Nepal to be with their families. They come to chase leads and to wait.

“My older cousin, he’s a doctor in Australia, and his wife is a dentist,” Saluja says. “So they both are coming back. They’re going to try with the search and to be with the family as well. They obviously want to be with the family.”

It’s been four days since the glacier collapsed high in the Himalayas, sending a wall of water, ice and mud down to destroy everything in its path.

The number of people killed has risen to 669, with nearly 3,000 people lost. On the Chinese side, more than 550 people are unaccounted for. Forty-two Australians are still missing, according to Dfat, including six identified as missing by Chinese authorities.

On Saturday, New South Wales man Michael Keats was confirmed to be one of them. He had reached the Nepal-Tibet border just moments before disaster struck, his family said in a statement.

View image in fullscreen Australian’s missing in Nepal. Clockwise from left - Karan Bhardwaj, Chitra Venkatraman, Venkatraman Balakrishnan, Sumi Adhikari and Family: Shylaja Muralitharan, Aarush Muralitharan, Ashwin Muralitharan & Chandrasekaran Muralitharan. Composite: Supplied by the families

“Confusion around the timing of the floods initially led us to believe our beautiful Michael would be safe in Kathmandu, preparing to fly home,” they said.

“Unfortunately, it was confirmed relatively quickly by the Isha Foundation that Michael and his Kailash travel group had arrived at Gyirong Port on the Nepal-Tibet border just 10 minutes before the tragic floods hit.”

Keats’ family said their thoughts and prayers were with everyone affected by the tragedy.

“[Michael] is gentle and kind, with a unique light that touches everyone lucky enough to know him,” they said.

Sagar Shrestha serves as the director of the Disaster and Crisis Management Department at the Nepal Red Cross Society in Kathmandu. He said the death toll could climb into the thousands.

A map showing the flood zone in Nepal

“But they are still finding survivors,” he says. “Some of them are being found in the jungle; they’ve gone up the mountain and are being helicoptered out.”

He said there were 14 hydropower plants along the river, six of which were under construction. It’s believed people could still be alive in the majority of them.

One of the key issues has become “the dignified management of the dead”, he says, as morgues and hospitals have filled up in some areas. According to local media, officials in the Chitwan district will collect DNA samples from 229 bodies that are starting to decay and are no longer identifiable, before burying them.

“It is now the major concern,” Shrestha says. “And the second thing is that if we are not being able to manage the dead bodies, there could be some kind of health issues.”

Since the crisis started, Sagar Pandey has barely slept. Pandey, the chief executive of the Himalaya Glacier Company, says 47 people from the trekking service are lost, including 15 Australians.

He had Australians in two different locations: five people 1.5km from the border of Tibet and Nepal, who were meant to be coming back that morning after breakfast and another 10 who had left the Syabrubesi valley and were driving towards the border checkpoint.

“I believe they were trapped because all three cars and jeeps are missing,” he says. “There were a total of 14 people: three drivers and then one guide and 10 Australians.”

How the deadly Nepal and Tibet flash flood unfolded – a visual guide Read more

Pandey has been spending his days going between the hospitals and checking in with the morgues to see if anyone on his tours has shown up. He is contacting family members of loved ones who are overseas and helping those who have just arrived. He has also been grieving his brother, who was guiding one of the treks.

On Wednesday, he chartered a helicopter to the disaster zone – he could see about 800 people standing on the mountain, who have all been rescued now, he says.

“There is a very low chance of survival that someone can still be alive,” he says. “The next process is to find the body if possible.”

There has been one glimmer of hope – on Saturday afternoon the foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, announced Australian woman Cara Severino was found safe after consular officials worked out where she was, and reached her via four-wheel drive.

View image in fullscreen Australian woman Cara Severino, who had been unaccounted for following the devastating floods along the Nepal-China border, was safely located. Photograph: Office of Senator Penny Wong

In a statement, Severino said she got out safely by teaming up with other survivors and using a tractor to drive out of the national park.

“My heart goes out to all the Nepalese families who are grieving loved ones,” she said. “We passed a guy hiking up to Thulu Safru who lost his whole family when their whole town was destroyed. It’s just so devastating and undeserving.”

“I feel for the families of those still missing; I know how much my family and friends went through.”

On Saturday afternoon, the Australian ambassador to Nepal, Simon Ernst, was waiting at the airport. Six more members of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s crisis response team had just arrived to help.

“There is a lot of damage to infrastructure, damage to power generation capability, damage to phone lines, telegraph poles, so communications is out,” he says. “Even the Nepali forces have lost contact with some of their personnel.

“Given the nature of search, rescue, and recovery operations, there are people in the water, in the mud. They’re obviously in danger should further flooding occur, and we can get heavy rainfall at any time given the monsoon.”

The disaster unfolded over three Nepalese districts – the one closest to Kathmandu has been the easiest to conduct search and rescue operations, because the accessibility is better and the valley is wider. Most Australians were last heard from in the top district, which was hit first by the flood.

No one knows how long it will take to search the area and find everyone, Ernst says, but in the event an Australian is found, the embassy will be told immediately.

“We understand that this is an incredibly difficult situation for [families],” Ernst says. “They should feel confident that the Australian government and the Nepalese government are doing everything we can to find their loved ones.

“They are very welcome to maintain contact with the Department of Foreign Affairs through our contact numbers and our contact centre in Canberra. If they’re here in Kathmandu, they’re welcome to make contact directly with the embassy, including with me.”

शनिदिन न्यू साउथ वेल्स के आदमी माइकल कीट्स के सेहो ओहि मे सं एक होय के पुष्टि भेल छल. आपदा आबय सँ किछुए क्षण पहिने ओ नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा पर पहुँचल छलाह, हुनकर परिवार द्वारा विज्ञप्ति जारी कयल गेल अछि ।

फुलस्क्रीन मे छवि देखू नेपाल मे ऑस्ट्रेलियाई’क लापता. बामा से घड़ी की दिशा में - करण भारद्वाज, चित्र वेंकटरामन, वेंकटरामन बालकृष्णन, सुमी अधिकारी एवं परिवार : श्यालाजा मुरलीथरण, आरुष मुरलीथरण, आश्विन मुरलीथरण एवं चन्द्रसेकरण मुरलीथरण | समग्र : परिवार द्वारा आपूर्ति

ओ सब कहलनि जे, बाढ़िक समय के आसपास भ्रम के कारण शुरू मे हमरा सब के विश्वास भ गेल जे हमर सुंदर माइकल काठमांडू मे सुरक्षित रहत, घर उड़बाक तैयारी मे।

“दुर्भाग्यवश ईशा फाउंडेशन द्वारा अपेक्षाकृत जल्दी पुष्टि भेल जे माइकल आ हुनकर कैलाश यात्रा समूह नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा पर ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह पर दुखद बाढ़ि सँ मात्र 10 मिनट पहिने पहुँचल छल।”

कीट्स केरऽ परिवार न॑ कहलकै कि हुनकऽ विचार आरू प्रार्थना ई त्रासदी स॑ प्रभावित सब के साथ छै ।

ओ सब कहलनि जे, [माइकल] कोमल आ दयालु छथि, एकटा अनूठा प्रकाश के संग जे हुनका जानय के भाग्यशाली सब गोटे के छूबैत अछि।

सागर श्रेष्ठ काठमांडू स्थित नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीमे आपदा आ संकट प्रबन्धन विभागके निदेशकके रुपमे कार्यरत अछि । ओ कहलनि जे, मृतकक संख्या हजारों मे चढ़ि सकैत अछि।

नेपालक बाढ़ि क्षेत्र देखबैत एकटा नक्शा

ओ कहैत छथि जे मुदा एखनो बचि गेल लोक ताकि रहल छथि। “किछु जंगल मे भेटि रहल अछि; पहाड़ पर चढ़ि गेल छथि आ हेलीकॉप्टर स’ बाहर निकालल जा रहल छथि.”

ओ कहला जे नदी क कात मे 14टा जलविद्युत संयंत्र अछि, जाहि मे स छहटा निर्माणाधीन अछि। मानल जाइत अछि जे एहि मे सं अधिकांश मे लोक एखनो जीवित भ’ सकैत अछि.

हुनकऽ कहना छै कि एकरऽ एगो प्रमुख मुद्दा “मृतकऽ के गरिमामय प्रबंधन” बनी गेलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि कुछ क्षेत्रऽ म॑ मुर्दाघर आरू अस्पताल भरलऽ छै । स्थानीय मीडिया के अनुसार चितवन जिला के अधिकारी 229 लाश के डीएनए नमूना संकलन करत जे सड़य लागल अछि आओर आब पहचान नहि भ रहल अछि, ओकरा दफनाबय सं पहिने.

श्रेष्ठ कहैत छथि जे आब इ प्रमुख चिंता अछि। “आरू दोसरऽ बात ई छै कि अगर हम्में मृत शरीर के प्रबंधन नै करी रहलऽ छियै त॑ कोनो तरह के स्वास्थ्य संबंधी मुद्दा भी आबी सकै छै।”

skip past newsletter promotion मुफ्त समाचार पत्र | हर सप्ताह के दिन मॉर्निंग मेल पर साइन अप करू हमर ऑस्ट्रेलियाई भोरका ब्रीफिंग दिन के प्रमुख कहानी के तोड़ैत अछि, जे अहां के बताबैत अछि जे की भ’ रहल अछि आओर ई किएक महत्वपूर्ण अछि अपन ईमेल दर्ज करू न्यूजलेटर प्रचार के बाद साइन अप करू

जहिया स संकट शुरू भेल अछि तहिया स सागर पांडे कए मुश्किल स नींद आबि गेल अछि। हिमालय ग्लेशियर कंपनी के मुख्य कार्यकारी पाण्डेय के कहनाय छनि जे ट्रेकिंग सेवा सं 47 लोक के नुकसान भ गेल अछि जाहि मे 15 ऑस्ट्रेलियाई सेहो शामिल छथिन्ह.

हुनका दू अलग-अलग स्थान पर ऑस्ट्रेलियाई छलनि : तिब्बत आ नेपालक सीमा सं डेढ़ किलोमीटर दूर पांच गोटे, जे ओहि दिन भोरे नाश्ता केलाक बाद वापस आबय वाला छलाह आ आओर 10 गोटे जे स्याब्रुबेसी घाटी सं निकलि सीमा नाका दिस गाड़ी सं जा रहल छलाह.

ओ कहैत छथि जे हमरा विश्वास अछि जे ओ सब एहि लेल फंसल छल जे तीनू गाड़ी आ जीप गायब अछि। “कुल १४ गोटे छल: तीन टा ड्राइवर आ फेर एकटा गाइड आ १० गोटे ऑस्ट्रेलियाई।”

नेपाल आ तिब्बत के घातक फ्लैश फ्लड केना खुलल – एक दृश्य मार्गदर्शक Read more

पाण्डेय अस्पताल के बीच जा क मुर्दाघर मे चेक इन करैत दिन बिताबैत रहलाह अछि जे हुनकर दौरा मे कियो आबि गेल अछि कि नहि. ओ विदेश मे रहनिहार प्रियजन के परिवार के सदस्य सं संपर्क क रहल छथिन्ह आओर एखनहि आयल लोक के मदद क रहल छथिन्ह. एकटा ट्रेक के मार्गदर्शन करय वाला अपन भाई के सेहो शोक मना रहल छथिन्ह.

बुधदिन ओ आपदा क्षेत्र मे हेलीकॉप्टर चार्टर कए लेलथि – ओ पहाड़ पर करीब 800 लोक कए ठाढ़ देख सकैत छलाह, जे सब कए आब बचाउल गेल अछि, ओ कहैत छथि।

ओ कहैत छथि जे एहि मे जीवित रहबाक संभावना बहुत कम अछि जे कियो एखनो जीवित रहि सकैत अछि। “अगिला प्रक्रिया अछि जँ संभव हो तऽ लाश खोजब।”

आशा केरऽ एगो झलक सामने ऐलऽ छै – शनिदिन दुपहर म॑ विदेश मंत्री पेनी वोंग न॑ घोषणा करलकै कि ऑस्ट्रेलियाई महिला कारा सेवेरिनो न॑ कांसुलर अधिकारियऽ न॑ ई पता लगाय क॑ कि हुनी कहाँ छै, आरू फोर-व्हील ड्राइव के माध्यम स॑ हुनका पास पहुँचलै ।

View image in fullscreen ऑस्ट्रेलियाई महिला कारा सेवेरिनो, जे नेपाल-चीन सीमा पर आयल विनाशकारी बाढ़ि के बाद बेहिसाब भ गेल छल, सुरक्षित स्थान पर आबि गेल छल. फोटोग्राफ : सीनेटर पेनी वोंग के कार्यालय

एक बयान मँ सेवेरिनो नँ कहलकै कि हुनी अन्य बची गेलऽ लोगऽ के साथ मिल क॑ ट्रैक्टर के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ नेशनल पार्क स॑ बाहर निकली क॑ सुरक्षित रूप स॑ बाहर निकली गेलै ।

ओ कहलीह जे हमर हृदय ओ सब नेपाली परिवार क प्रति दुखी अछि जे अपन प्रियजन कए शोक संतप्त अछि। “हम एकटा एहन लड़का के पास स’ गुजरि गेलहुँ जे थुलु सफ्रू धरि पैदल चलैत छल जे अपन पूरा परिवार के गमा लेलक जखन ओकर पूरा शहर तबाह भ’ गेलै. ई त’ बस एतेक विनाशकारी आ अयोग्य अछि.”

“हमरा एखनो लापता लोकक परिवारक प्रति अनुभूति होइत अछि;हमरा बुझल अछि जे हमर परिवार आ मित्र कतेक गुजरल।”

शनिदिन दुपहर मे नेपाल मे ऑस्ट्रेलियाक राजदूत साइमन अर्नस्ट एयरपोर्ट पर प्रतीक्षा मे छलाह । विदेश आरू व्यापार विभाग केरऽ संकट प्रतिक्रिया टीम केरऽ छह आरू सदस्य अभी-अभी मदद करै लेली पहुँचलऽ छेलै ।

ओ कहैत छथि जे बुनियादी ढांचा कए काफी नुकसान भेल अछि, बिजली उत्पादन क्षमता कए नुकसान भेल अछि, फोन लाइन, टेलीग्राफ क खंभा कए नुकसान पहुंचल अछि, ताहि लेल संचार बंद अछि। ओ कहलनि जे, नेपाली सेना तक अपन किछु जवान सं संपर्क खत्म भ गेल अछि।

“सर्च, रेस्क्यू, आरू रिकवरी ऑपरेशन केरऽ प्रकृति क॑ देखत॑ हुअ॑ पानी म॑, थाल म॑ लोग छै । जाहिर अछि जे जँ आओर बाढ़ि आबि जाय त’ ओकरा सभ केँ खतरा छैक, आ मानसून केँ देखैत हमरा सभ केँ कोनो समय भारी बरखा भ’ सकैत अछि.”

ई आपदा नेपाली तीन जिला – काठमांडू के सबसे नजदीक के जिला खोज-बचाव के काम करना सबसें आसान रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि सुलभता बेहतर छै आरू घाटी चौड़ा छै । अधिकांश ऑस्ट्रेलियाई केरऽ आखिरी बार शीर्ष जिला म॑ सुनलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा प॑ सबसें पहल॑ बाढ़ केरऽ असर पड़लऽ छेलै ।

अर्नस्ट के कहनाय छनि जे एहि इलाका के तलाशी लेबय आओर सभ के खोजय मे कतेक समय लागत, मुदा अगर कोनो ऑस्ट्रेलियाई मिलय त दूतावास के तुरंत बता देल जाएत.

अर्नस्ट कहैत छथि जे हम सब बुझैत छी जे [परिवार] लेल इ अविश्वसनीय रूप स कठिन स्थिति अछि। ओ कहलनि जे, हुनका सब के विश्वास महसूस करबाक चाही जे ऑस्ट्रेलिया सरकार आ नेपाल सरकार अपन प्रियजन के खोजय लेल हर संभव प्रयास क रहल अछि।

“हमरऽ संपर्क नंबर आरू कैनबरा म॑ हमरऽ संपर्क केंद्र के माध्यम स॑ विदेश विभाग स॑ संपर्क बनाबै लेली हुनकऽ बहुत स्वागत छै । अगर हुनी यहाँ काठमांडू म॑ छै त॑ हुनका सीधा दूतावास स॑ संपर्क करै के स्वागत छै, जेकरा म॑ हमरा भी शामिल छै ।”

full_article:
Nepalese Houston man speaks on flood aftermath FOX 26's Mekenna Earnhart spoke to the president of the Nepalese Association of Houston about the devastating floods in his home country. He says he was in the country's capital at the time of the floods, but the capital was not affected.

The Brief NAH President Gyanshor Shrestha witnessed live news of 100-meter floodwaves in Nepal hours before his flight back to Houston, prompting local leaders to immediately organize a candlelight vigil and launch relief efforts upon his return. The floodwaters destroyed key national highways, bridges, and hydropower plants across several districts, isolating entire valley communities and destroying local farmland. Community leaders are urging Houstonians to open their wallets and share the verified GoFundMe Campaign to support both immediate search-and-rescue assistance and long-term infrastructure reconstruction.



Catastrophic flash flooding leaves a trail of destruction

The backstory:

HOUSTON, Texas - As catastrophic flash flooding leaves a trail of destruction along the Nepal–China border, members of Houston’s Nepalese community are rallying from afar to mobilize emergency aid for victims and displaced families.

The disaster struck on Aug. 26 when a massive high-altitude glacier collapse and ice-rock avalanche tore through the Lhende Khola and Bhote Koshi river system. The resulting wall of water, mud, and debris swept away critical bridges, highways, and villages across several districts, including Rasuwa and Nuwakot, before swelling the Trishuli River downstream.

According to the Associated Press, the combined death toll in Nepal and Tibet has climbed near 700, with more than 3,000 people still reported missing. The destruction of key trade corridors and hydropower infrastructure has left remote mountain settlements isolated and hundreds of thousands without basic services.

Nepalese Association of Houston

Local perspective:

At Kathmandu Curry and Bar in Houston, leaders of the Nepalese Association of Houston (NAH) gathered to coordinate local relief efforts and raise awareness for loved ones thousands of miles away.

Gyanshor Shrestha, President of the Nepalese Association of Houston, was in Nepal when the disaster unfolded.

"I found out I was trying to get lunch around 11 o'clock. We saw on the TV breaking news, keep flashing," Shrestha said. "I saw the glacier lake burst out... and there is a force, you can see 100 meters, like that, the waves. It's coming from the upper hill to the downward. It's scary to see that."

Shrestha was scheduled to fly back to Texas the same afternoon, watching live coverage up until he had to board his flight.

"It was so sad to leave in that situation, when people are dying, people are missing, and we don't know what's going to happen downstream to more small villages," Shrestha recalled. "As soon as I got here, we did a candlelight vigil for those who died... Nepal needs help now. Please help."

Aires Kheral, Vice President of the Nepalese Association of Houston, was at work in Texas when he first learned of the flash floods and immediately started checking on contacts back home.

"Every hour, worse and worse pictures came through," Kheral said. "There are hydropower projects on that river valley that have people who work in those places. We just tried to find out what happened."

Kheral noted that while the initial emergency response is taking place on the ground, long-term disaster recovery will require sustained international backing.

"Right now, the emergency is being taken care of locally. But there's a lot of work coming up—people have to rebuild, people have to find jobs, farms, roads, bridges," Kheral said. "So if we can focus on getting the funds together right now and send it to the right place, that would be a lot of help."

The collapse wiped out critical infrastructure along national transit corridors, severing cross-country routes and isolating key valley communities. Local leaders emphasize that the loss of life and geography destroyed by the wall of mud will impact the region for years.

"We know that some community members here have had relatives and farmland in the affected area, and somebody told me that they had lost their farm," Kheral said. "They're not going to get it back because that mountain is gone."

For members of the Greater Houston Nepalese community, the imagery brings back memories of past natural disasters, including major regional earthquakes and smaller flood events.

"Not even three years ago, in the same place, the same thing happened—but not on this large scale," Shrestha said.

Support relief operations

What you can do:

To support relief operations, the Nepalese Association of Houston—alongside the Creative Nepalese Society, Gulmi Samaj Houston, and the Greater Houston Nepalese Chamber of Commerce—has launched an official Emergency Relief Fund.

Community leaders urge Houstonians to assist by donating or sharing the verified fundraising campaign online:

Campaign: Nepal Flood Relief Emergency Fund

Organized By: Nepalese Association of Houston (NAH)

GoFundMe Link: http://gofund.me/4b9f44758

"At last, we request all the people, whoever can, open their wallet now," Shrestha said. "Nepal needs help now in the recovery process. Please spread that word to the entire community."

The Source: Gyanshor Shrestha, Aires Kheral, The Associated Press (AP), Nepalese Association of Houston (NAH)

बाढ़ के बाद नेपाली ह्यूस्टन के आदमी न॑ बतैलकै फॉक्स २६ केरऽ मेकेना अर्नहार्ट न॑ अपनऽ देश म॑ आबै वाला विनाशकारी बाढ़ के बारे म॑ नेपाली एसोसिएशन आफ ह्यूस्टन के अध्यक्ष स॑ बात करलकै । हुनकर कहनाय छनि जे बाढ़ि के समय ओ देश के राजधानी मे छलाह, मुदा राजधानी पर कोनो असर नहि पड़ल.

ब्रीफ एनएएच के अध्यक्ष ज्ञानशोर श्रेष्ठ अपन वापस ह्यूस्टन के उड़ान सं घंटों पहिने नेपाल मे 100 मीटर के बाढ़ के लहर के लाइव खबर देखलखिन्ह, जाहि सं स्थानीय नेता सभ तुरंत मोमबत्ती के रोशनी मे जागरण के आयोजन केलनि आ वापसी पर राहत कार्य शुरू केलनि. बाढ़ के पानी स॑ कई जिला म॑ प्रमुख राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग, पुल, आरू जलविद्युत संयंत्र नष्ट होय गेलै, जेकरा स॑ पूरा घाटी समुदाय अलग-थलग होय गेलै आरू स्थानीय खेती के जमीन नष्ट होय गेलै । समुदाय के नेता ह्यूस्टन के लोगऽ स॑ आग्रह करी रहलऽ छै कि वू अपनऽ बटुआ खोल॑ आरू सत्यापित गोफंडमी अभियान क॑ साझा करी क॑ तत्काल खोज-बचाव सहायता आरू दीर्घकालिक बुनियादी ढाँचा के पुनर्निर्माण दूनू के समर्थन करी सक॑ ।



विनाशकारी झटका बाढ़ि विनाशक निशान छोड़ि जाइत अछि

बैकस्टोरी : १.

ह्यूस्टन, टेक्सास : नेपाल-चीन सीमा पर विनाशकारी फ्लैश फ्लडिंग स॑ तबाही के निशान बनलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, त॑ ह्यूस्टन केरऽ नेपाली समुदाय के सदस्य पीड़ित आरू विस्थापित परिवारऽ लेली आपातकालीन सहायता जुटाबै लेली दूर स॑ जुटी रहलऽ छै ।

ई आपदा 26 अगस्त क॑ तखनिये आबी गेलऽ छेलै जब॑ उच्च ऊंचाई प॑ ग्लेशियर केरऽ भारी ढहना आरू बर्फ केरऽ चट्टान केरऽ हिमस्खलन ल्हेंडे खोला आरू भोटे कोशी नदी प्रणाली क॑ फाड़ी देलकै । एकरऽ परिणामस्वरूप पानी, थाल आरू मलबा केरऽ दीवार न॑ रसुवा आरू नुवाकोट सहित कई जिला केरऽ महत्वपूर्ण पुल, राजमार्ग, आरू गाँव क॑ बहाय देलकै, जेकरा बाद त्रिशुली नदी क॑ नीचें फूली गेलै ।

एसोसिएटेड प्रेस के अनुसार नेपाल आ तिब्बत मे संयुक्त मृत्यु के संख्या 700 के करीब बढ़ि गेल अछि, जखन कि एखनो तीन हजार सं बेसी लोक के लापता होय के खबर अछि. प्रमुख व्यापारिक गलियारा आरू जलविद्युत बुनियादी ढाँचा के नष्ट होय के कारण दूरस्थ पहाड़ी बस्ती अलग-थलग होय गेलऽ छै आरू लाखों लोग बुनियादी सेवा के बिना छै ।

नेपाली एसोसिएशन ऑफ ह्यूस्टन

स्थानीय परिप्रेक्ष्य : १.

ह्यूस्टन के काठमांडू करी एंड बार में नेपाली एसोसिएशन ऑफ ह्यूस्टन (एनएएच) के नेता सब स्थानीय राहत प्रयास के समन्वय आ हजारों मील दूर अपन प्रियजन के लेल जागरूकता पैदा करय लेल जुटल छलाह.

नेपाली एसोसिएशन अफ ह्यूस्टन के अध्यक्ष ज्ञानशोर श्रेष्ठ जखन आपदा के खुलासा भेल छल तखन नेपाल मे छलाह.

श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, हमरा पता चलल जे हम 11 बजे के आसपास लंच लेबय के कोशिश क रहल छी, टीवी पर ब्रेकिंग न्यूज देखलहुं, चमकैत रहू। "हम देखलियै जे ग्लेशियर झील फाटि गेलै... आओर एकटा बल छै, 100 मीटर, ओहिना, लहरि देखबा मे अबैत अछि. ई ऊपरका पहाड़ी सँ नीचा दिस आबि रहल अछि. से देखब डरावना अछि."

श्रेष्ठ क॑ वू ही दुपहर म॑ वापस टेक्सास लेली उड़ान भरना छेलै, जब॑ तलक ओकरा अपनऽ फ्लाइट म॑ नै चढ़ै के जरूरत छेलै, लाइव कवरेज देखतै ।

श्रेष्ठ स्मरण करैत कहलनि जे, ओहि स्थिति मे छोड़ब एतेक दुखद छल, जखन लोक मरि रहल अछि, लोक गायब भ रहल अछि, आ हमरा सब कए नहि पता जे नीचा आओर छोट गाम मे की होएत। "हमरा एत' पहुँचैत देरी हम सभ मरि गेल लोकक लेल मोमबत्तीक रोशनी मे जागरण केलहुं... नेपाल केँ आब मदद चाही. कृपया मदद करू."

नेपाली एसोसिएशन ऑफ ह्यूस्टन के उपाध्यक्ष आयर्स खेरल टेक्सास में काज पर छलाह जखन हुनका पहिल बेर फ्लैश फ्लड के जानकारी भेटलनि आ तुरंत घर वापसी में संपर्क के जांच करय लगलाह.

खेरल कहलनि जे, हर घंटा खराब सं खराब तस्वीर आबि रहल छल। "ओहि नदी घाटी पर जलविद्युत परियोजना अछि जाहि मे ओहि ठाम काज करय वाला लोक अछि. हम सब बस इ पता लगेबाक कोशिश केलहुं जे की भेल।"

खेरल न॑ नोट करलकै कि जब॑ कि प्रारंभिक आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया जमीन प॑ ही होय रहलऽ छै, लेकिन दीर्घकालिक आपदा स॑ उबर॑ लेली लगातार अंतरराष्ट्रीय समर्थन के जरूरत होतै ।

खेरल कहलनि जे, एखन इमरजेंसी के स्थानीय स्तर पर ध्यान राखल जा रहल अछि, मुदा बहुत काज आबि रहल अछि-लोक के फेर सं बनाबय पड़त, लोक के नौकरी, खेत, सड़क, पुल खोजय पड़त. "त' जँ हम सभ एखनहि फंड केँ एक ठाम जमा करबा पर ध्यान द' सकब आ ओकरा सही जगह पर पठा सकब त' ई बहुत मददगार होयत."

ई पतन स॑ राष्ट्रीय पारगमन गलियारा के साथ महत्वपूर्ण बुनियादी ढाँचा के सफाया होय गेलै, जेकरा स॑ क्रॉस-कंट्री मार्ग क॑ टूटी गेलै आरू प्रमुख घाटी समुदाय क॑ अलग करी देलऽ गेलै । स्थानीय नेता सब एहि बात पर जोर दैत छथि जे थाल के देबाल स नष्ट भेल जान आ भूगोल के नुकसान एहि क्षेत्र पर सालों तक पड़त।

खेरल कहला जे हमरा सब कए पता अछि जे एहि ठामक किछु समुदाय क लोक क प्रभावित इलाका मे रिश्तेदार आ खेत क जमीन रहल अछि, आ कियो हमरा कहलक जे हुनकर खेत गंवा देल गेल अछि। "ओ पहाड़ खतम भ' गेलाक कारणेँ ओकरा सभ केँ वापस नहि भेट' बला अछि।"

ग्रेटर ह्यूस्टन नेपाली समुदाय के सदस्यऽ लेली ई बिम्बऽ स॑ पिछला प्राकृतिक आपदा के याद आबी जाय छै, जेकरा म॑ प्रमुख क्षेत्रीय भूकंप आरू छोटऽ-छोटऽ बाढ़ के घटना भी शामिल छै ।

श्रेष्ठ बजलीह, "तीन साल पहिने सेहो नहि, एकहि ठाम, एके बात भेल छल-मुदा एतेक पैघ पैमाना पर नहि।"

राहत अभियान के समर्थन करब

अहाँ की क' सकैत छी:

राहत अभियानऽ के समर्थन करै लेली ह्यूस्टन केरऽ नेपाली एसोसिएशन-क्रिएटिव नेपाली सोसाइटी, गुल्मी समाज ह्यूस्टन, आरू ग्रेटर ह्यूस्टन नेपाली व्यापार मंडल के साथ-साथ आधिकारिक आपातकालीन राहत कोष शुरू करलकै ।

समुदाय के नेता ह्यूस्टन के लोगऽ स॑ आग्रह करै छै कि सत्यापित धन उगाही अभियान क॑ ऑनलाइन दान करी क॑ या साझा करी क॑ सहायता करलऽ जाय:

अभियान : नेपाल बाढ़ राहत आपातकालीन कोष

आयोजना: नेपाली एसोसिएशन ऑफ ह्यूस्टन (NAH)

गोफंडमी लिंक: http://gofund.me/4b9f44758

श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, अंततः हम सब लोक स आग्रह करैत छी, जे कियो भ सकैत अछि, आब अपन बटुआ खोलू। "नेपाल केँ आब रिकवरी प्रक्रिया मे मदद चाही। कृपया ओहि बात केँ समस्त समाज मे पसारब।"

• Rescue effort: A search is underway for almost 900 missing employees at various hydropower projects in Nepal after Wednesday’s catastrophic flooding on its border with China. Emergency workers have pumped air into one tunnel but have yet to establish communication with anyone inside.

• Search continues: Around 3,000 people, including Americans and other foreigners, are still missing. The US is providing $3.6 million of humanitarian aid, up from the earlier announced $500,000.

• Grim toll: More than 670 people have died in Nepal and at least 16 were killed in China. Nepali authorities are struggling to cope with the mounting number of bodies, and Chinese officials have said there have been no more survivors found yet.

• Agonizing wait: Loved ones gather daily at medical centers and morgues to search for information on victims. Families in the US and across the world await word on missing travelers.

title: Nepal To Bury Unidentified Flood Victims. How They Will Be Identified Later - NDTV
description: Nepal To Bury Unidentified Flood Victims. How They Will Be Identified Later  NDTV
publisher.title: NDTV
full_article:
Nepal has said it will start burying unidentified and unclaimed bodies recovered after the devastating flash floods tore through the country this week, citing the risk of infection and the deteriorating condition of the remains.

At least 675 bodies have so far been recovered since the tsunami-like rumble of water and mud struck villages and towns on Wednesday morning. Chitwan, a district in the south that borders India, recovered the most number of bodies at 233.

Chitwan has been struggling to prevent the corpses from decomposing due to a lack of adequate space and facilities at hospitals. The authorities in the district on Saturday decided to bury the bodies after health experts warned that the increasing decomposition and foul smell from the bodies kept under temporary arrangements could increase the risk of infection.

ALSO READ | Before Nepal Flood, A Glacial Fall: Tracing The Trigger, A 100-km Killer Surge

"As the number of dead bodies piled up, we used a house as a cooling centre where the bodies were kept," an official said.

"As the house also ran out of space, we had no alternative but to bury them," the official added.

DNA Samples Collected From Bodies

The officials have been collecting DNA samples from the bodies before burying them.

They are also maintaining records using identification or reference numbers to facilitate possible identification in the future.

Each body has a unique identification number with its location tag so that relatives can exhume them once DNA matches.

By Saturday afternoon, DNA profiling for over 100 bodies had been completed, and they were ready for burial.

1.5-Metre Deep Burial Pits

The burial pits are being dug to a depth of 1.5 metres to ensure the bodies can be easily exhumed later. A 40-centimetre gap has been maintained between them to ensure that only the specific body identified via DNA matching can be retrieved.

The bodies are being packed into bags with an identification number. A concrete platform with a signboard is being constructed at each burial site that will display the body's identification number.

Plans are also in place to document the burial process through video and photography and to geo-tag the burial site.

People looking for their missing relatives will be required to provide DNA samples at various hospitals across the country. Once the DNA test results are available, Nepal's health department will match them with the DNA from the bodies to identify the specific body number. Based on that number, the police will consult the records to determine the exact location where the body was buried.

The bodies will then be exhumed and handed over to them.

The police have also uploaded details of unidentified and unclaimed bodies on a website.

full_article:
Bay Area Nepalese man talks about floods impact on family & friends North Bay man from Nepal with family and friends still there , shares photos and videos of the devastation captured by his loved ones who survived. A man in Kathmandu describes the many families search for the missing.

The Brief A massive wall of rock, ice, mud, and debris crashed along the Nepal-China border, wiping out entire villages and leaving the Bay Area's Nepalese community anxiously awaiting news of loved ones. Jay Tamang, a North Bay resident and native of Nepal, has confirmed his immediate family survived, but is still waiting to hear from dozens of other relatives and friends. Tamang's nonprofit, Nepal Freed, which previously built three schools after the 2015 earthquake, is organizing relief efforts to help families devastated by the floods.



MARIN COUNTY, Calif. - The devastating images of riverside towns north of Kathmandu swept away by massive walls of rock, ice, and mud have hit close to home in the Bay Area.

North Bay resident Jay Tamang watched the disaster unfold through videos and photos sent by his family and friends in Nepal.

Bay Area Nepalese community reacts to catastrophic flooding

While Tamang's immediate family survived the disaster, their homes were swept away, and he remains unable to contact dozens of other relatives and friends.

"Relatives, friends... people from my village are affected," Tamang said. "We're really sad. We don't know how many people are missing."

Ground zero: connecting with survivors in Kathmandu

Through a video call, Tamang connected KTVU with Agbir Lama, a survivor in Kathmandu who recently returned from an impacted area after helping move his sister's children to safety.

Lama described the scene as "like a dream" with entire cities and buildings swept away.

Lama praised the rescue efforts despite limited infrastructure.

"The army, they are really doing a good job," Lama said. "Still our country is a developing country. We don't have a lot of infrastructure. We don't have a lot of technology, but still they are trying to find people, they are trying to save the people there."

Lama plans to ride his motorbike back into the impacted areas in the coming days to search for dozens of other relatives he has not yet been able to contact.

How to Help

Tamang is mobilizing support through his nonprofit, Nepal Freed, which he originally established following Nepal's massive 2015 earthquake—raising $150,000 to build three schools in his village and a neighboring area.

He is now coordinating relief efforts for families who lost their homes.

For more information on Nepal Freed: http://www.nepalfreed.com

Amber Lee is a reporter with KTVU. Reach Amber at Amber.Lee@Fox.com, text/leave a message at 510-599-3922, or follow her on Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter @AmberKTVU.Tiktok @amberleenews

As rescue teams searched for missing people following catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border, Earth scientists reviewed satellite imagery for clues to the cause and assessed the devastation.

The flooding Wednesday killed hundreds of people in Nepal and Tibet, and hundreds more are missing, including foreigners and pilgrims.

Geomorphologists Kristen Cook and Dan Shugar said initial images from Nepal were obscured by clouds and dust from the debris, so they could only see that part of a glacier had broken off from Langtang Lirung peak, near the border with Tibet. "It shows the whole area without anything hidden, and we could see that, yes, it looked like there was not only this glacier that had failed, but a much larger chunk of the bedrock of the mountainside itself that had given way," said Shugar, associate professor at the University of Calgary. "You have this big bedrock failure that took part of the glacier with it."

Shugar said it's heart-wrenching to look downstream from there on the images, to where people were living, and see how the debris has buried villages.

After slamming to the valley floor, the debris maintained its momentum through the steep, narrow valley as ice melted, said Cook, at the Université Grenoble Alpes in France. Water and mud several stories high swept through communities.

The Trishuli River surged during the flooding. Before and after satellite images of the Kolpurtar, Betrawati and Syapru Besi areas of Nepal show that the river is now much wider, and brown and black, because it overtopped its banks in some areas and filled with debris in others. The change in the color of the water shows how much sediment the flow was carrying, turning from greenish to very brown because it's full of mud, Cook said.

Towns and villages that were devastated along the river banks are submerged in debris and mud. They appear as areas of brown. Some houses are still poking through in an image of the Betrawati area.

This satellite image provided by Vantor shows a cement site in Nepal on Oct. 18, 2023.

The flooding toppled and swept away buildings in Syapru Besi, a popular tourist spot where a famous trek to Langtang begins. In before-and-after images, a side river is now wider too, because the flow was so powerful it pushed upstream.

The flooding "left a wasteland in its wake" that will take many years to recover from, said Alton Byers, a mountain geographer at the University of Colorado at Boulder. Byers lived in Nepal and now returns there yearly to study glacial hazards and work with communities to prepare. This is the largest glacier flood he has seen, by far.

Byers, a faculty research scientist at the university's Institute of Arctic and Alpine Research, said he thinks Wednesday's flooding is related to climate change. The Earth's warming is melting glaciers and permafrost, causing instability and the breakage of massive amounts of snow and ice at high altitudes. That can be a catalyst for a series of cascading events, he said.

What we know — and don’t know — about what caused the Nepal flood wave

"All the indicators, to me, point to the impacts of warming trends," he said. "In this case, the permafrost that for millennia has helped to hold together high-altitude rock and ice and soil and glaciers is now weakening and becoming unstable."

Cook and Shugar said that at this point, they can't say for sure there's a direct link to climate change. Slopes fail and landslides happen, Cook said, though permafrost is melting and that is destabilizing mountainsides.

"While we cannot at this point directly link this collapse to climate change, it is not unexpected to see more events of this type with a warming climate," Cook said. "Not this big, hopefully not this big."

फ्रांस केरऽ यूनिवर्सिटी ग्रेनोबल आल्प्स म॑ कुक न॑ कहलकै कि घाटी केरऽ तल प॑ झटका लगला के बाद मलबा न॑ खड़ा, संकीर्ण घाटी के माध्यम स॑ अपनऽ गति क॑ बरकरार रखलकै, कैन्हेंकि बर्फ पिघली गेलै । पानि आ थाल कतेको मंजिला ऊँच समुदाय मे बहैत छल ।

बाढ़ि के दौरान त्रिशुली नदी उफान पर आबि गेल। नेपाल केरऽ कोलपुरतर, बेतरवती आरू स्याप्रू बेसी क्षेत्र केरऽ उपग्रह स॑ पहलऽ आरू बाद के तस्वीर स॑ पता चलै छै कि ई नदी अब॑ बहुत चौड़ा होय गेलऽ छै, आरू भूरा आरू कारी रंग के होय गेलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि ई कुछ क्षेत्रऽ म॑ अपनऽ किनारे स॑ ऊपर आबी गेलऽ छेलै आरू कुछ क्षेत्र म॑ मलबा स॑ भरलऽ छेलै । कुक न॑ कहलकै कि पानी के रंग म॑ बदलाव स॑ पता चलै छै कि ई बहाव कतेक तलछट क॑ ल॑ जाय रहलऽ छेलै, जे हरियर स॑ बहुत भूरा रंग म॑ बदली जाय छै, कैन्हेंकि ई कीचड़ स॑ भरलऽ छै ।

नदीक कात मे जे शहर-गाम तबाह भ गेल छल, ओ मलबा आ थाल मे डूबल अछि। भूरा रंगक क्षेत्रक रूपमे देखाइत अछि । किछु घर एखनो बेतरवती इलाका क छवि मे पोकिंग क रहल अछि।
